entries.what: Lets the phone act as a webcam for a PC and supplies video-call effects.
entries.loses: You lose 'use phone as webcam' and Smart Connect video effects.

entries.label: Moto
entries.what: The 'Moto' app -- the hub where you turn Moto features on and off: gestures, display extras, personalisation shortcuts.
entries.loses: You lose the settings screens for Moto features. Gestures already switched on generally keep working while com.motorola.actions is installed, but you can no longer change them.

entries.label: Moto Care
entries.what: The older Moto Care support app, which lives alongside Device Help on current firmware.
entries.loses: You lose a second, largely redundant support entry point.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Background support component for Moto Care.
entries.loses: Nothing beyond Moto Care itself. Remove with com.motorola.motocare.

entries.label: CQATest
entries.what: A hidden factory hardware-test menu (reached by typing a secret code in the dialler), used on the production line and in service centres.
entries.loses: The hidden hardware-test menu is gone. Diagnostics only -- no everyday feature depends on it. Note: this is the package people mean by 'com.motorola.motocit'; it is diagnostics, not something load-bearing.

entries.label: Moto Display
entries.what: The older standalone Moto Display / Peek Display app that showed notifications on a sleeping screen.
entries.loses: Peek/always-on notification previews are lost. On the Edge 50 Fusion this standalone package is absent -- the feature has moved inside com.motorola.moto and the system UI -- so your phone probably has no such app.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Moto Power Touch -- lets you assign actions to different presses of the power button.
entries.loses: Custom power-button actions are lost. Not found in current Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Controls Moto's edge-lighting effects -- the coloured glow around the screen edge for calls and notifications.
entries.loses: Edge lighting stops. Community reports link this package to some display-brightness behaviour, so check adaptive brightness after removing it.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Not an ordinary app at all -- on the Edge 50 Fusion this is a signed system module (an APEX) that ships Moto Secure's system-level service code.
entries.loses: System modules of this kind cannot be uninstalled per-user and attempting to interfere with them risks an unbootable phone. If your debloater lists it, hide it or mark it undeletable.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: The engine behind Moto Secure's App Lock -- it holds the app-lock credential and enforces which apps need a PIN or fingerprint.
entries.loses: App Lock stops protecting apps, and if it is removed while apps are locked you can be left unable to reach the settings that unlock them. Turn App Lock off in Moto Secure first, then disable.

entries.label: MotoSignatureApp
entries.what: Declares Motorola's private permissions -- the internal rules that let Moto system apps talk to each other.
entries.loses: Other Motorola apps can lose permissions they expect and misbehave in ways that are hard to trace back. Some debloat lists suggest removing it; the safer route is to leave it, or disable and watch for oddities.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: A second-generation version of Motorola's internal permission declarations.
entries.loses: Same as com.motorola.motosignature.app -- Moto apps may lose internal permissions. Prefer leaving it in place.

entries.label: Moto Tour
entries.what: A guided tour app that shows you how to use the phone.
entries.loses: The tour is gone. Not found in Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Dual SIM settings
entries.what: Provides the dual-SIM screens and logic -- which SIM makes calls, which carries data, SIM naming.
entries.loses: Dual-SIM management breaks: you may be unable to choose which SIM is used for calls or mobile data. On a two-SIM phone this is effectively a telephony break.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: A configuration overlay for the dual-SIM screens; on the Edge 50 Fusion it appears to be an unused single-SIM variant.
entries.loses: Probably nothing, but it sits next to telephony configuration, so disable rather than uninstall and check calls and data on both SIMs afterwards.

entries.label: MyKey
entries.what: Motorola's feature for assigning custom actions and usage restrictions to keys and device functions.
entries.loses: Custom key actions set through MyKey stop working. Rarely used on this model.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Motorola's support components for NFC (tap-to-pay, tag reading).
entries.loses: NFC features can stop working, including contactless payment. Not found in the current Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Records when the mobile network requests the phone's location, for the carrier-location entry in Settings.
entries.loses: You lose a rarely-read information screen about carrier location requests. Emergency location services do not depend on it.

entries.label: Moto Unplugged
entries.what: Moto Unplugged -- a focus/digital-wellbeing mode where you choose which apps and interruptions are allowed while you switch off.
entries.loses: You lose the Moto Unplugged focus mode; Android's own Focus Mode and Do Not Disturb remain. IMPORTANT NAMING CORRECTION: Moto Unplugged's real package is com.motorola.om (confirmed by its Google Play listing). The plausible-looking 'com.motorola.unplugged' does not exist -- do not ship it. Older debloat lists describe com.motorola.om vaguely as 'operational management', which is wrong.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Carrier device-management/provisioning client used to switch operator services on and off remotely.
entries.loses: Rarely used on unbranded phones. Carrier-side service activation (mostly a US thing) would stop working.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Motorola's configuration for Android System Intelligence, the Google component behind Live Caption, smart replies and now-playing.
entries.loses: Android System Intelligence features (Live Caption, smart text selection, notification replies) may stop working properly.

entries.label: PAKS Finance
entries.what: Motorola's device-financing enforcement app ('kiosk' lock). On phones bought on an instalment plan it can lock the phone if payments stop.
entries.loses: On a financed or instalment-plan phone, tampering with the financing lock can lock or disable the device, or breach the finance agreement. On a fully-paid retail phone it lies dormant and removing it gains nothing. Motorola marks its companion notification package non-disableable. Leave it alone.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: The notification component of Motorola's device-financing lock.
entries.loses: Same risk as com.motorola.paks. Motorola explicitly flags this one as non-disableable in the Edge 50 Fusion firmware, so treat it as protected.

entries.label: Personalise
entries.what: The theming engine behind Personalise -- accent colours, fonts, icon shapes, wallpaper-based colour schemes.
entries.loses: You lose Motorola's theming screen and may be stuck with whatever theme is currently applied. Confirmed present on the Edge 50 Fusion.

entries.label: Moto Photo Editor
entries.what: Motorola's photo editing app.
entries.loses: You lose Motorola's photo editor; Google Photos editing is unaffected. Not present in current Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Part of Motorola's mechanism for automatically installing a set of partner apps when the phone is first set up or reset.
entries.loses: After a factory reset the phone would not silently reinstall the partner app bundle -- usually the point of removing it. No everyday feature is lost.

entries.label: Programming Menu
entries.what: A hidden developer/service menu opened with a dialler code.
entries.loses: The hidden menu is unavailable. Not present in current Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Configures RCS -- the modern chat features (typing indicators, read receipts, high-quality images) inside Google Messages.
entries.loses: RCS chat features in Google Messages may stop working or fail to re-register, leaving you on plain SMS.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: A small helper used only during first-boot setup.
entries.loses: Nothing after setup is complete, but it may be needed again after a factory reset. Disabling is reversible; prefer that over uninstalling.

entries.label: Screenshot editor
entries.what: The editor that pops up after a screenshot, including long/scrolling screenshots of whole web pages.
entries.loses: Screenshots still work, but you lose the crop/annotate pop-up and scrolling screenshots. Genuinely useful -- not routine bloat.

entries.label: Secure Folder
entries.what: An encrypted folder for hiding photos, files and apps behind a separate PIN.
entries.loses: Anything stored inside Secure Folder can become permanently unreachable. Move everything out first; then disable rather than uninstall.

entries.label: Moto Secure
entries.what: The Moto Secure dashboard: PIN-pad scrambling, network protection, app lock and Secure Folder settings gathered in one place.
entries.loses: You lose the Moto Secure screen and its shortcuts. If you have put anything into Secure Folder or set up App Lock, deal with that FIRST -- see com.motorola.securevault and com.motorola.motosecurecore.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: An extension component of the Moto Secure dashboard.
entries.loses: Parts of the Moto Secure screen may be missing or empty. Remove alongside com.motorola.securityhub, not on its own.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Listed in the Android Debloat List with the label 'System update' and a caution flag; its exact role could not be confirmed.
entries.loses: UNVERIFIED -- this package could not be confirmed in Edge 50 Fusion firmware, and the one list that mentions it associates it with system updates. Given the possible update impact, do not offer it for removal without device-level confirmation.

entries.label: Setup
entries.what: Motorola's addition to the first-run setup wizard (the screens you see when you switch the phone on for the first time).
entries.loses: Almost nothing visible day-to-day, but the Universal Android Debloater project warns that freezing this package stops Google Play system updates (Project Mainline), which means missed monthly security fixes. The Android Debloat List disagrees and calls it removable. Given the near-zero benefit, leave it alone.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Motorola's motion and position service: it works out whether the phone is face-down, in a pocket, or being picked up.
entries.loses: Gestures and screen behaviours that depend on movement or pocket detection (lift to check, flip to silence, some display wake behaviour) become unreliable. It does use location services, which is why some people remove it.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Battery-saving logic that drops the phone from 5G to 4G when 5G is not useful.
entries.loses: Battery life on 5G can get noticeably worse, and network switching behaviour changes. It touches radio selection, so disable only.

entries.label: Smart Feed
entries.what: Motorola's built-in content and promotion feed -- 'suggested apps' in the app drawer, sponsored recommendations, and lock-screen content.
entries.loses: You lose 'Suggested apps' in the Moto app drawer and Motorola's promotional content. This app was found in 2025 to be routing app launches through affiliate-tracking links (Motorola called it unintended and fixed it), and users report notable background data use -- a strong candidate for removal.

entries.label: Family Space
entries.what: A child-friendly mode: you pick which apps a child may use and how long for.
entries.loses: Family Space is gone. Only matters if you hand the phone to a child; Google Family Link does the same job.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Provides Motorola's spatial-sound (surround) audio effect.
entries.loses: Spatial audio stops working and some audio-effect settings may vanish. Because this is an audio effects provider, disable rather than uninstall.

entries.label: Moto Note
entries.what: Moto Note -- Motorola's handwriting and sketching notebook, built for stylus phones.
entries.loses: Handwritten notes app is gone; export anything you want to keep first. The Edge 50 Fusion has no stylus and this app is not in its firmware, so it is probably absent.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: A Motorola background service that other Moto features call into; it is also tied to the reliability of the chop-for-torch gesture.
entries.loses: The fast torch gesture can become inconsistent and other Moto features may lose a helper they expect. Disable rather than uninstall.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: The desktop-style taskbar and interface used when the phone is connected to an external screen.
entries.loses: Desktop mode on an external monitor loses its taskbar. If you never plug the phone into a screen, nothing changes.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Watches the phone's temperature and throttles or shuts it down before it overheats.
entries.loses: Overheating protection is weakened -- a genuine hardware-safety and battery risk. Never remove.

entries.label: Moto Widget
entries.what: The Moto clock-and-weather home-screen widget.
entries.loses: The Moto clock/weather widget vanishes from the home screen and leaves a gap where it was. Any other clock widget works fine.

entries.label: Time Zone Data
entries.what: Keeps time-zone information up to date so the clock is right when you travel.
entries.loses: Documented to cause a boot loop on at least one Moto model. Not present on the Edge 50 Fusion, but keep the 'never' rating for safety.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Reports daily Wi-Fi usage statistics to Motorola.
entries.loses: Nothing -- it is telemetry only. Wi-Fi itself is untouched.

entries.label: Mobile Device Information Provider
entries.what: A background Amazon component preinstalled on some phones under partner deals. It has no icon and its purpose is device-information reporting rather than anything you use.
entries.loses: Amazon apps stop being installed automatically. Note that Motorola marks this package non-disableable, so 'disable' will be refused and uninstall-for-user is the only route.

entries.label: Amazon Prime Video
entries.what: Amazon's video streaming app, commonly preinstalled under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose Prime Video. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Amazon Shopping
entries.what: Amazon's shopping app (global build), commonly preinstalled under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose the Amazon app. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Amazon Music
entries.what: Amazon's music streaming app, sometimes preinstalled.
entries.loses: You lose Amazon Music. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Aura
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- the Lenovo-branded build of the same Aura silent installer. Motorola is a Lenovo subsidiary, so this variant occasionally appears on Motorola builds.
entries.loses: Unsolicited installs stop. No genuine feature is lost. Can return after a major system update.

entries.label: MotoApps
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- a silent app installer. Aura is an advertising company's on-device platform that Motorola is paid to preinstall. During or after setup it installs sponsored apps and games you did not choose, and nags you with notifications to accept more.
entries.loses: You stop getting unsolicited app and game installs and their notifications. No genuine phone feature is lost. Warning: this is a system app, so a major system update or a factory reset can bring it back -- re-check after any big Android update.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: Dolby's own audio-processing engine that the Dolby Atmos screen controls; it sits in the phone's audio path.
entries.loses: Removing an audio-effects engine can leave apps with no working audio output, and on some Moto models audio-effect removal causes a boot loop. Leave it and disable the Dolby settings app instead if you want it out of the way.

entries.label: Mobile Services Manager
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- a silent app installer with a deliberately official-sounding name. Made by the advertising company Digital Turbine, it downloads, installs and updates sponsored apps in the background without asking you, and holds a very large set of permissions.
entries.loses: Apps stop appearing on your phone by themselves. Nothing you use is lost. Warning: it is a system app and can be restored by a major system update or factory reset, so re-check after updates. Removing it for the current user is enough to stop it running day to day.

entries.label: Meta App Installer
entries.what: A hidden background updater that Meta pays phone makers to preinstall. It downloads and installs updates to Facebook, Instagram and Messenger outside the Play Store. It is not the Facebook app itself and has no icon.
entries.loses: Nothing you can see stops working. If you later install Facebook or Instagram from the Play Store, they update normally through Google Play instead. May be restored by a major system (OTA) update or a factory reset -- removing for the current user is enough day to day, but re-check after any big Android update.

entries.label: Facebook
entries.what: The full Facebook social-network app, preinstalled under a commercial deal rather than because the phone needs it.
entries.loses: You lose the Facebook app. You can reinstall it any time from the Play Store, where you will get a normal user-installed copy that is fully removable.

entries.label: Meta Services
entries.what: A hidden Meta background service that runs whether or not you ever sign in to Facebook. It supports Meta's location/nearby-places and analytics features for the Meta apps.
entries.loses: No visible feature is lost. Facebook and Instagram still work if you install them yourself. Can return after a major system update.

entries.label: Meta App Manager
entries.what: An empty 'stub' app whose only job is to install the full Facebook app and nudge you to use it. It has no user interface of its own.
entries.loses: You simply stop being prompted to install Facebook. Nothing else changes. Can return after a major system update.

entries.label: Glance
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- the notorious Motorola lock-screen advertising platform, shipped as 'GlanceSpacesMotorola'. It takes over your lock screen with sponsored news, games and ads. Turning it off in Settings often results in full-screen prompts asking you to switch it back on.
entries.loses: Your lock screen goes back to a normal wallpaper and notifications. Nothing you need is lost. Warning: the app file stays in the phone's read-only system area, so a factory reset or a major system update can bring it back. It is also worth turning off its two hidden switches (the secure settings state_glance_lockscreen and state_space_lockscreen) alongside removal.

entries.label: Indus Appstore
entries.what: An Indian third-party app store (by PhonePe) preloaded on Indian Motorola units.
entries.loses: You lose an alternative app store you almost certainly never use. The Play Store is unaffected.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- an installer component from the advertising company InMobi (the same group behind Glance).
entries.loses: Nothing you would miss -- it exists to install promoted apps. Confirmed in the Indian Edge 50 Fusion firmware.

entries.label: Rescue Security
entries.what: LogMeIn Rescue remote-support tool that allows a Motorola agent to view and control the phone during a support session.
entries.loses: Motorola support can no longer take remote control of your phone. Many people remove it on privacy grounds.

entries.label: Link to Windows
entries.what: Connects the phone to a Windows PC for messages, photos and calls. On some phones this is a genuine, deeply integrated feature rather than bloatware.
entries.loses: The 'Link to Windows' feature in Quick Settings stops working. If you use Phone Link on a Windows PC, keep it.

entries.label: Microsoft 365 / Office Mobile
entries.what: Microsoft's combined Word, Excel and PowerPoint app, sometimes preinstalled.
entries.loses: You lose the Office app. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Microsoft Outlook
entries.what: Microsoft's email and calendar app, sometimes preinstalled under Microsoft's OEM deals.
entries.loses: You lose Outlook. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Make sure any email accounts set up only in Outlook are moved first.

entries.label: Microsoft OneDrive
entries.what: Microsoft's cloud storage app, sometimes preinstalled under Microsoft's OEM deals.
entries.loses: You lose the OneDrive app. Files already in OneDrive stay in your account. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: PayJoy's financing-lock app, preloaded on some Motorola units sold on instalment plans; it can lock the phone for non-payment.
entries.loses: Removing it on a financed phone can lock the device or breach the finance contract. Motorola marks it non-disableable and non-force-stoppable. Present in the global Edge 50 Fusion firmware; not seen in the Indian build.

entries.label: Runs in the background
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- a background advertising module from Taboola that pushes a lock-screen stories feed of low-quality ads and articles. Uses background data and nags the user.
entries.loses: The lock-screen story feed and its background data use stop. Nothing you need is lost.

entries.label: Amazon Shopping (India build)
entries.what: The Amazon India build of the shopping app, found on Indian retail units -- which is also what many Bangladeshi grey-market and official units are.
entries.loses: You lose the Amazon India app. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Qualcomm DCF
entries.what: An empty Qualcomm package with no code, related to Bluetooth content sharing on paper only.
entries.loses: Nothing changes -- the package contains no working code.

entries.label: Qualcomm Diagnostic Services
entries.what: A tiny diagnostics collector that starts at boot and when the phone is plugged into a computer.
entries.loses: No visible change. Only used for hardware data collection.

entries.label: Qualcomm Data Power Manager
entries.what: Qualcomm's Data Power Manager service, believed to manage power efficiency of the modem and data connection. Its exact job is not publicly documented.
entries.loses: Because nobody can say for certain what it does, removing it risks worse battery life on mobile data, or data connection problems. Disable and watch for a few days before considering anything more.

entries.label: Qualcomm LTE Broadcast Manager
entries.what: The manager component for LTE Broadcast (see eMBMS above).
entries.loses: Same as eMBMS -- you lose an operator feature that is not used in Bangladesh or India. Calls and mobile data are unaffected.

entries.label: Qualcomm Phone / IMS Service
entries.what: Qualcomm's telephony and IMS (internet-based calling) helper that sits between Android's dialler and the modem.
entries.loses: Can break VoLTE (calls over 4G), VoWiFi (calling over Wi-Fi) and in some cases calling altogether. Some users report calls still work after removal, but this is device-dependent and not worth the risk. If it must be touched, disable rather than uninstall so it can be re-enabled.

entries.label: Qualcomm Primary Card Controller
entries.what: Controls SIM detection and which SIM is the primary one on some Qualcomm-based phones.
entries.loses: SIM detection and dual-SIM switching can break. Rated unsafe by community lists.

entries.label: Qualcomm QCC
entries.what: A newer (Android 13 onwards) Qualcomm logging and analytics component tied to Qualcomm Device Management and Analytics.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm Data Status Notification
entries.what: Shows warnings when you approach a mobile-data limit, and is tied into the chipset's data status reporting.
entries.loses: On some skins, disabling this has broken the whole mobile-network settings section and made SIMs show 'no service'. That is documented on Xiaomi's HyperOS rather than Motorola, so the Motorola behaviour is unknown -- treat as risky.

entries.label: Qualcomm Device Info
entries.what: A hidden device-information screen that is not exposed to users.
entries.loses: Settings > About phone still shows your device information -- that comes from elsewhere.

entries.label: Qualcomm Mobile Statistics Service
entries.what: Another network and app-usage statistics collector with no user-facing screen.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm Display Colour Management
entries.what: A colour-tuning tool for the display; on most phones it is dormant and any colour modes you see come from the phone maker's own settings.
entries.loses: No visible change on most phones. If screen colours change, re-install it.

entries.label: Qualcomm AT Command Forwarder
entries.what: Passes low-level 'AT' commands between Android and the modem -- the old modem control language.
entries.loses: Community lists rate it removable, but it sits on the modem control path. On a phone you rely on for calls, disable and test calls, SMS and data before going further.

entries.label: Qualcomm Content Adaptive Backlight (CABL)
entries.what: Adjusts screen contrast and backlight based on what is on screen, to save power. Not the same as automatic brightness.
entries.loses: Slightly higher screen power use, but colours may look more accurate. Automatic brightness is unaffected.

entries.label: Qualcomm eMBMS (LTE Broadcast)
entries.what: Support for LTE Broadcast, a way for mobile networks to send the same video or data to many phones at once. Almost no operator in South Asia uses it.
entries.loses: You lose LTE Broadcast, which you almost certainly never use. It runs at boot but not continuously, so the battery gain is small. Normal calls and data are unaffected.

entries.label: Qualcomm Interface Permissions
entries.what: A completely empty placeholder package.
entries.loses: Nothing changes.

entries.label: Qualcomm Location Service (IZat / GNSS Assistance)
entries.what: Qualcomm's assisted-GPS service. It downloads predicted satellite data so GPS locks on in seconds instead of minutes. It also periodically sends a device ID, your location and nearby cell towers and Wi-Fi networks to Qualcomm's servers, which is why privacy lists flag it.
entries.loses: GPS may still work but can take minutes instead of seconds to get a fix, and some apps may fail to get a location at all. Reports also exist of boot loops when this is removed together with Android's fused location provider. If privacy is the concern, prefer denying it network and location access, or disabling it, rather than uninstalling.

entries.label: Qualcomm IZat XT
entries.what: A hidden companion to Qualcomm's location service, part of the IZat/XTRA assisted-location system that reports location data back to Qualcomm.
entries.loses: Mainly a privacy gain. Some risk of slower GPS fixes. Disable first and check that maps and navigation still find you quickly.

entries.label: Qualcomm IZat XT Setup
entries.what: The one-time setup/consent screen for Qualcomm's IZat location service. Hidden from the app list.
entries.loses: No visible change. It only ever shows a legal notice.

entries.label: Qualcomm RIL Message Tunnel
entries.what: A message channel between Android and the Qualcomm modem, used for SIM, SMS and 5G signalling -- especially on dual-SIM phones.
entries.loses: Reported to break calls after a reboot on some phones, and to stop 5G working on the second SIM. The Edge 50 Fusion is a dual-SIM device, so this is a real risk. Disable only, never uninstall, and re-enable at the first sign of call or SIM trouble.

entries.label: Qualcomm Auto Registration
entries.what: Collects device activation data to register the warranty remotely. In 2019 a version of this package was caught sending IMEI and SIM identifiers unencrypted to a server in China on Nokia phones; the maker called it a mistake.
entries.loses: No visible change. Warranty registration is normally handled by Motorola's own account app instead.

entries.label: Qualcomm Call Enhancement
entries.what: Claims to improve call audio quality. It also has call-recording capability, and a 2019 vulnerability (CVE-2019-15472) allowed unauthorised microphone recording through it.
entries.loses: Call audio may sound slightly different. Because it touches the call path, disable first and make a test call before considering full removal.

entries.label: Qualcomm Carrier Configure
entries.what: Applies operator-specific network configuration on phones that use Qualcomm's own version of this component.
entries.loses: Mobile data, MMS and VoLTE settings for your operator can break. Unlikely on a Motorola but must never be offered for removal.

entries.label: Qualcomm Connectivity Engine (CNE)
entries.what: Manages the hand-off between mobile data and Wi-Fi and picks the better-performing connection -- the machinery behind settings such as 'automatically switch to mobile data when Wi-Fi is poor'.
entries.loses: Wi-Fi and mobile data can both become noticeably less reliable, with the phone clinging to a dead Wi-Fi network instead of switching to mobile data. Best left in place.

entries.label: Qualcomm Device Statistics Service
entries.what: Records statistics about how you use the phone -- data, Wi-Fi, battery, app usage, messages sent.
entries.loses: No visible change. Android's own battery and data screens are separate.

entries.label: Qualcomm Extended Settings
entries.what: On phones that use Qualcomm's own settings replacements, this is needed for the Wi-Fi hotspot.
entries.loses: Hotspot may break. Rated 'unsafe' by community lists. Unlikely on a Motorola.

entries.label: Qualcomm Adreno GPU Drivers (name ends in a chipset codename)
entries.what: The graphics drivers for the Adreno GPU, shipped as an updatable app. The real package name always has a chipset codename and Android version appended, for example com.qualcomm.qti.gpudrivers.pineapple.api34 -- the exact suffix for the Snapdragon 7s Gen 2 in the Edge 50 Fusion is not something we could source, so the app must match on the com.qualcomm.qti.gpudrivers. prefix rather than a hard-coded name.
entries.loses: Removing the GPU driver package can leave the phone unable to draw the screen -- a black screen or boot loop. Never offer any package starting com.qualcomm.qti.gpudrivers. for removal.

entries.label: Qualcomm IMS Settings
entries.what: A hidden settings screen for IMS (internet-based calling). The only user-facing option it exposes is auto-rejecting incoming calls.
entries.loses: Community lists rate this safe to remove, but it sits inside the IMS/calling stack, so on a phone you rely on for calls the cautious move is to disable rather than uninstall and confirm VoLTE still works.

entries.label: Qualcomm Local Profile Assistant (eSIM)
entries.what: Handles eSIM profiles -- downloading and switching between operator subscriptions stored in the phone rather than on a plastic SIM.
entries.loses: eSIM setup and switching can stop working. Harmless to lose if you only ever use physical SIM cards, but the Edge 50 Fusion's eSIM support varies by region, so do not assume.

entries.label: Qualcomm Modem Test Mode
entries.what: An engineering tool for testing the modem. Not reachable in normal use.
entries.loses: No visible change. It is a test harness, not part of the live modem path.

entries.label: Qualcomm Network Settings (hidden)
entries.what: A hidden engineering menu for choosing network modes (2G/3G/4G only) and toggling VoLTE.
entries.loses: You lose a hidden diagnostic menu, and possibly the VoLTE toggle on some builds. Not worth touching.

entries.label: Qualcomm Performance Dump
entries.what: A developer logging tool that dumps performance information about running services.
entries.loses: No visible change. Only useful to engineers.

entries.label: Qualcomm Power-off Alarm
entries.what: Lets an alarm wake the phone from a powered-off state.
entries.loses: Alarms may no longer sound if the phone is switched off. Minor, but worth knowing if you rely on alarms.

entries.label: Qualcomm QCC Auth Manager
entries.what: Part of Qualcomm's analytics/feedback stack; not reachable by users.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm QCC Network Statistics
entries.what: Collects network usage statistics for Qualcomm analytics. Android's own data-usage screen does not depend on it.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm QColor
entries.what: A Qualcomm enhanced-colour service that no app appears to use.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm Device Management and Analytics (QDMA)
entries.what: Collects logs, crash reports and network data for Qualcomm.
entries.loses: No visible change. Less background data collection.

entries.label: Qualcomm QMMI Hardware Test
entries.what: The factory/service-centre test app used to check that the screen, speakers, sensors and so on work. Hidden from users.
entries.loses: A repair shop would lose one diagnostic tool. Nothing you use is affected.

entries.label: Qualcomm QMS Connection Security
entries.what: Another Qualcomm telemetry service, documented as connecting in the background to a Qualcomm telemetry host.
entries.loses: No visible change. Purely reduces background data and reporting.

entries.label: Qualcomm QMS Credentials Service
entries.what: Part of Qualcomm's Quality Management Service family; community analysis found only logging code.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm QMS Telemetry
entries.what: Sends diagnostic and usage telemetry to Qualcomm's servers. Purely data collection -- no user-facing feature.
entries.loses: Nothing stops working. You stop sending diagnostics to Qualcomm.

entries.label: Qualcomm QMS TrustZone Access
entries.what: Despite the security-sounding name, community analysis found it only logs secure-area access rather than providing it.
entries.loses: No visible change reported. The actual secure hardware is in firmware, not this app.

entries.label: Qualcomm Quick Settings (mobile data)
entries.what: Provides the mobile-data quick-settings tile on phones that use Qualcomm's replacements for standard Android components.
entries.loses: You may lose the ability to turn mobile data on and off. Unlikely on a Motorola.

entries.label: Qualcomm RCS/IMS Bootstrap Utility
entries.what: Sets up RCS -- the newer chat standard that replaces SMS in Google Messages.
entries.loses: RCS chat features (typing indicators, read receipts, high-quality media in Google Messages) may stop working. Plain SMS is unaffected.

entries.label: Qualcomm Secure Camera Service
entries.what: A background service that community analysis found only collects camera data rather than providing camera function.
entries.loses: The camera itself is unaffected. If you notice any camera fault, re-install it.

entries.label: Qualcomm System Helper Service
entries.what: A privileged background service with power, phone-state and settings permissions. Its purpose is not clearly documented.
entries.loses: On at least one Xiaomi device, uninstalling it stopped apps running at all. Unknown on Motorola. Leave it in place.

entries.label: Qualcomm SIM Contacts
entries.what: A hidden tool for reading and editing contacts stored on the SIM card.
entries.loses: You may lose the option to import contacts from a SIM. Most people never use this.

entries.label: Qualcomm Technology Reporting (QTR/SMQ)
entries.what: Sends hardware and software configuration and performance data to Qualcomm. Contains a hidden 'Hardware Feedback' consent screen.
entries.loses: No visible change. Stops the hardware feedback reporting.

entries.label: Qualcomm Telephony Service
entries.what: Handles voice processing during phone calls on Qualcomm chipsets. This is core call machinery, not an app.
entries.loses: Removing or disabling this can stop phone calls working, or make callers unable to hear you. The Motorola Edge 50 Fusion uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon 7s Gen 2, so this package applies to it. Do not offer this for removal.

entries.label: Qualcomm Tether Service
entries.what: On some phones (mostly Chinese brands that use Qualcomm's own versions of standard apps) this provides Wi-Fi hotspot/tethering.
entries.loses: Wi-Fi hotspot and USB tethering can stop working. Unlikely to be present on a Motorola, which uses Android's standard tethering, but if it is present, do not remove it.

entries.label: Qualcomm UCE Shim Service
entries.what: A translation layer between Android's IMS stack and the Qualcomm modem, used for RCS chat, VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling.
entries.loses: Likely to break RCS chat, VoLTE, Wi-Fi calling and some operator settings. Not worth removing.

entries.label: Qualcomm UIM Remote SIM Lock Service
entries.what: Background service related to SIM/R-UIM cards and remote SIM locking.
entries.loses: Mostly relevant to operator-locked handsets. Small risk to SIM handling -- disable rather than uninstall.

entries.label: Qualcomm UIM GBA Service
entries.what: SIM-card authentication helper (GBA -- generic bootstrapping architecture), used by some operator services.
entries.loses: Some operator authentication services could fail. Rarely used outside operator-specific apps.

entries.label: Qualcomm Workload Classifier
entries.what: Categorises running apps, most likely so the chipset can schedule CPU work efficiently.
entries.loses: Possible worse performance or battery life. Its exact role is not publicly documented, so treat with caution.

entries.label: Qualcomm aptX ALS
entries.what: A hidden Bluetooth audio test/sample component for Qualcomm's aptX codecs. The actual aptX codec support lives in the Bluetooth stack, not here.
entries.loses: Bluetooth audio quality is unaffected in reports. If your headphones lose aptX, re-install it.

entries.label: Qualcomm Bluetooth Dual-SIM Call Handling
entries.what: Hidden Bluetooth call handling (answer, hang up, conference) for dual-SIM phones.
entries.loses: On at least one device, disabling this forced all call audio out of the earpiece regardless of the speaker/Bluetooth choice. Test a Bluetooth call before keeping it disabled.

entries.label: Qualcomm Sunlight Visibility Improvement
entries.what: A hidden display-enhancement setting not exposed to users.
entries.loses: No visible change reported.

entries.label: Qualcomm Time Service
entries.what: Keeps the clock correct across reboots by remembering the offset between your set time and the chipset's own clock.
entries.loses: The clock may drift or reset to a wrong time after a reboot, which in turn can break secure connections, banking apps and alarms. Very little to gain -- leave it alone unless you have a specific reason.

entries.label: Qualcomm Wi-Fi Display Service
entries.what: Provides Miracast -- casting your screen to a TV over Wi-Fi Direct.
entries.loses: Screen casting to a TV over Miracast stops working. Casting through Chromecast/Google Home is separate and unaffected.

entries.label: Qualcomm Voice Assist / Voice Activation
entries.what: Always-listening voice wake-word detection from Qualcomm, running constantly in the background.
entries.loses: Any chipset-level voice wake word stops working. Google Assistant's own 'Hey Google' is separate and unaffected.

entries.label: UC Browser
entries.what: A web browser with a long history of privacy and security problems, occasionally preinstalled in South and Southeast Asia.
entries.loses: You lose UC Browser. Any other browser still works.

entries.label: Adobe Scan
entries.what: Document scanning and PDF app, named in reviews as a preinstall on Motorola Edge 50-series retail units.
entries.loses: You lose Adobe Scan. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list, so package name verified from the Play Store listing instead.

entries.label: Agoda
entries.what: Hotel and flight booking app, sometimes preinstalled in Asian markets under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose Agoda. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the Play Store listing. We could not confirm it ships on the Edge 50 Fusion.

entries.label: Aura for Motorola (alternate build)
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- the same Aura silent-installer platform, shipped under a Motorola-specific package name on some builds. Shows a persistent notification until you agree to install games.
entries.loses: Unsolicited game installs and their nagging notification stop. No genuine feature is lost. Can return after a major system update.

entries.label: Booking.com
entries.what: Hotel-booking app, named in reviews as a preinstall on Motorola Edge 50-series retail units.
entries.loses: You lose the Booking.com app. Reinstallable from the Play Store or usable through a web browser.

entries.label: Digital Turbine Toolbar
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- an adware component from Digital Turbine used to showcase sponsored apps.
entries.loses: Sponsored app promotions stop. No genuine feature is lost.

entries.label: Temu
entries.what: Aggressive discount shopping app that has appeared as a paid preinstall on some budget and mid-range Android phones. Known for heavy notification and advertising behaviour.
entries.loses: You lose Temu and its notifications. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the Play Store listing. We could not confirm it ships on the Edge 50 Fusion specifically.

entries.label: TouchPal Emoji Keyboard
entries.what: A third-party keyboard whose maker was banned from Google Play in 2019 over advertising abuse. Occasionally preinstalled.
entries.loses: You lose this keyboard. Make sure another keyboard (such as Gboard) is set as your default first, or you will not be able to type. Removing a keyboard without a replacement active is one of the few genuinely disruptive removals.

entries.label: Dailyhunt
entries.what: Indian news-aggregator app, a frequent Indian preinstall. Heavy on notifications and advertising.
entries.loses: You lose Dailyhunt and its notifications. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Josh
entries.what: Indian short-video app, a frequent Indian preinstall alongside Dailyhunt.
entries.loses: You lose Josh. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the Play Store listing.

entries.label: Facebook Lite
entries.what: A cut-down Facebook app aimed at low-data markets. Often preinstalled instead of, or alongside, the full app on South Asian retail units.
entries.loses: You lose Facebook Lite. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Facebook Messenger
entries.what: Meta's chat app, sometimes preinstalled alongside the Facebook stubs.
entries.loses: You lose Messenger chat. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Flipkart
entries.what: Indian shopping app, preinstalled with ads on Indian retail units.
entries.loses: You lose Flipkart. Reinstallable from the Play Store; Flipkart does not deliver to Bangladesh.

entries.label: Glance (trending stories on lock screen)
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- another Glance build that pushes unsolicited 'trending' stories onto the lock screen.
entries.loses: Lock-screen story feed stops. Nothing you need is lost. Can return after a major system update.

entries.label: Instagram
entries.what: Meta's photo and video sharing app, preinstalled under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose Instagram. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: AppCloud (ironSource)
entries.what: HIGH-VALUE REMOVAL -- the older 'AppCloud' generation of the same advertising-company installer. It asks your age and gender, then pushes a list of apps to install at first setup.
entries.loses: You stop being pushed sponsored apps. No genuine feature is lost.

entries.label: LinkedIn
entries.what: Professional networking app, named in reviews as a preinstall on Motorola Edge 50-series retail units.
entries.loses: You lose the LinkedIn app. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Netflix
entries.what: The Netflix streaming app, preinstalled under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose Netflix. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Some preinstalled bundles include a free trial that is only redeemable through the preinstalled copy.

entries.label: Netflix Partner Activation
entries.what: A tiny helper whose job is to activate a preinstalled Netflix deal and place the Netflix icon on your home screen. Not the Netflix app itself.
entries.loses: You may lose an included Netflix trial offer, if any. The Netflix app itself still works and can be installed from the Play Store.

entries.label: Opera Branding Provider
entries.what: A small companion package that applies partner branding to the preinstalled Opera browser. No user-facing function.
entries.loses: No visible change.

entries.label: Opera Mini
entries.what: A data-saving web browser, preinstalled under commercial deals particularly in South Asia and Africa.
entries.loses: You lose Opera Mini. Any other browser (including Chrome) still works. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Opera Preinstall Data
entries.what: A hidden helper that exists only to tag the preinstalled Opera browser with tracking/attribution codes so Opera can be paid for the placement.
entries.loses: No visible change at all.

entries.label: PhonePe
entries.what: Indian UPI payments app, preinstalled on Indian retail units.
entries.loses: You lose PhonePe. If you have money or a linked bank mandate in it, check the account through another device or the web first. Reinstallable from the Play Store. UPI is India-only and of no use in Bangladesh.

entries.label: Spotify
entries.what: Music streaming app, commonly preinstalled under a commercial deal.
entries.loses: You lose Spotify. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Truecaller
entries.what: Caller ID and spam-call blocking app, very commonly preinstalled on South Asian retail units. It uploads contact and call metadata to build its directory, which is the main privacy concern.
entries.loses: You lose caller ID for unknown numbers and Truecaller's spam blocking. If it is your default dialler or SMS app, set another one first. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the Play Store listing.

entries.label: WhatsApp
entries.what: Meta's messaging app. Frequently preinstalled on Motorola retail units in South Asia.
entries.loses: You lose WhatsApp and its chat history unless you have a backup. Only remove this if you genuinely do not use it -- in Bangladesh and India it is often the main messaging app. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: TikTok
entries.what: Short-video app, named in reviews as a preinstall on Motorola Edge 50-series retail units.
entries.loses: You lose TikTok. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: ShareChat
entries.what: Indian regional-language social app, a frequent Indian preinstall.
entries.loses: You lose ShareChat. Reinstallable from the Play Store.

entries.label: Moj
entries.what: Indian short-video app from the ShareChat group, a frequent Indian preinstall.
entries.loses: You lose Moj. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the app's public documentation.

entries.label: Hotstar / JioHotstar
entries.what: Indian video streaming app, preinstalled on some Indian retail units. Note that Disney+ Hotstar and JioCinema merged into 'JioHotstar' in 2025, so the current package name and branding may have changed -- this needs re-checking against the live Play Store listing before shipping.
entries.loses: You lose the Hotstar app. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Because the app was rebranded, the package name here is not confirmed against a current source.

entries.label: Paytm
entries.what: Indian payments and wallet app, preinstalled on some Indian retail units.
entries.loses: You lose Paytm. Check for any wallet balance first. Reinstallable from the Play Store. Not in the UAD-NG list -- package name verified from the Play Store listing.
